mainTopic: Closing the sugya on contradicting witnesses in a סוטה case: following the majority when the witnesses are פסולי עדות, re-reading רבי נחמיה, and the הדרן for פרק מי שקינא
overview: The גמרא finishes its discussion of witnesses who contradict each other about a סוטה. It explains that the משנה is talking about a case where a woman, who is normally not a valid witness, testified first. So it re-reads רבי נחמיה's words: two women against one woman count like two men against one man, but two women against one valid man are only a half-and-half split. The גמרא then asks why the משנה needs two cases about פסולי עדות. It answers that the majority rule works in the strict direction and in the lenient direction too. The chapter מי שקינא then closes with the הדרן. The new chapter opens with a משנה listing texts that may be said in any language, and texts that must be said only in לשון הקודש. The משנה proves the Hebrew rule for ביכורים and חליצה from the words 'answer and say', and רבי יהודה brings his own proof from 'ככה'. It then begins describing the ceremony of the blessings and curses at הר גריזים and הר עיבל, and the writing of the תורה on stones in seventy languages. That description continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case is where a woman testified first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה is talking about a case where a woman, who is normally not a valid witness, was the first to testify.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what case are we dealing with here? A case where a woman came first and testified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains which situation the משנה is describing, so that the משנה fits with the earlier rule about the first witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said that when the תורה believes one valid witness, he counts like two, so nobody coming after him can outweigh him. That rule only works when a valid witness came first. Here a woman testified first, so her word does not have that power, and the later witnesses can be counted by majority.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with? (introduces an answer that narrows the case)
At first; from the start
A woman; here, a witness who is normally not valid for testimony

phrases.english: And here, what are we dealing with?
For example, where a woman came first.
phrases.notes: Since she was first, she does not get the power of a valid first witness, so the others who come after her can outweigh her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the earlier difficulty with the משנה, which carries over from the previous part of the daf, by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if the משנה clashed with the rule that a single valid first witness counts like two.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a case where a woman, not a valid witness, came first, so that rule does not apply.

steps.title: Re-reading the words of רבי נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: Because the case is about a woman testifying first, the גמרא adjusts the wording of רבי נחמיה: two women against one woman count like two men against one man, but two women against one valid man is only a tie.
steps.simpleTranslation: And adjust רבי נחמיה's statement to read like this: רבי נחמיה says: wherever the תורה believed one witness, follow the majority of opinions. And they made two women against one woman like two men against one man. But two women against one man is like half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the wording of רבי נחמיה's statement so that it fits the case it just described.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The majority rule is now limited to witnesses of the same kind: two women outweigh one woman. A valid man is worth a full witness, while each woman counts less, so two women against one man do not make a clear majority. It is a half-and-half split, and the משנה does not deal with that case.

keyTerms.meaning: And adjust it; read the text this way
The תנא whose opinion is being re-read
The majority of opinions; count the witnesses and follow the larger side
The תורה believed a single witness
Half and half; an even split

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that counting the majority is not just counting heads. Each witness's status matters, so a valid man is not outweighed by two women.

phrases.english: And adjust the statement of רבי נחמיה like this:
רבי נחמיה says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד —
phrases.english: Wherever the תורה believed one witness,
follow the majority of opinions.
And they made two women against one woman
like two men against one man.
But two women against one man
is like half and half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 1: since the case is a woman testifying first, רבי נחמיה's wording must match.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adjusting the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי נחמיה's words seemed to let two women outweigh one valid man.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two women outweigh one woman. Two women against one valid man is an even split.

steps.title: Why two cases about invalid witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs two separate cases to teach that we follow the majority among witnesses who are not valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need two cases about witnesses who are not valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה lists two cases that seem to teach the same idea. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both clauses of the משנה seem to teach the same thing: with פסולי עדות, follow the larger side. If one case is enough, the second looks extra. The גמרא wants to know what the second case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are not valid witnesses
Why do I need it? Why is this needed?
Two (cases)

phrases.english: And why do I need two cases about those invalid for testimony?
phrases.notes: He means the two clauses of the משנה, where one side has one witness and the other side has two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the משנה is understood as being about invalid witnesses, the גמרא asks why it needs two cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second case about invalid witnesses adds

steps.title: Majority works both strictly and leniently
steps.stepSummary: The second case is needed so we do not think the majority rule applies only in the strict direction. The משנה teaches that it applies in the lenient direction too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we follow the majority of opinions only to be strict, but to be lenient we do not follow it. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each case teaches something different. One shows the majority rule working toward a strict result, the other toward a lenient result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without both cases, we might think the majority of invalid witnesses counts only when it makes things stricter for the woman. The second case shows that the majority counts even when it leads to a lenient result. So there is no difference, and we always follow the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
In the strict direction
In the lenient direction
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.whatToRemember: With witnesses who are not valid, we follow the majority whether it leads to a strict result or a lenient one. That is why the משנה needs both cases.

phrases.english: You might have said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָזְלִינַן בָּתַר רוֹב דֵּיעוֹת לְחוּמְרָא,
phrases.english: when we follow the majority of opinions, it is to be strict,
but to be lenient, we do not follow it.
So it teaches us otherwise.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two cases are needed. One shows the majority rule works for a strict result, and the other shows it works for a lenient result as well.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter מי שקינא
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the chapter מי שקינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter מי שקינא.
steps.whatsHappening: This line formally closes the chapter מי שקינא. The next chapter begins after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional closing that marks the end of a פרק. It expresses our wish to come back and learn the chapter again. It does not add any new law.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (traditional closing of a chapter)
Name of the chapter: one who warned his wife

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter מי שקינא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after its last sugya.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter מי שקינא is complete.

steps.title: Things that may be said in any language
steps.stepSummary: The new chapter opens with a list of seven things that may be said in any language.
steps.simpleTranslation: These may be said in any language: the סוטה portion, the declaration of tithes, קריאת שמע, תפלה, ברכת המזון, the oath of testimony, and the oath about a deposit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter and a new משנה begin here. The משנה lists texts that a person may say in any language he understands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chapter starts with פרשת סוטה, which ties it to the topic of the whole מסכת. The point of the list is that for these texts, saying them in Hebrew is not required. Saying them in another language still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: These are said. These are the opening words and the name of the new chapter.
In any language
The declaration a person makes saying he gave all his tithes properly
The oath of testimony, sworn by a witness who denies knowing testimony
The oath about an object someone was given to guard

phrases.english: These are said in any language:
the portion of the סוטה, and the declaration of tithes,
קריאת שמע, and prayer, and Grace after Meals,
and the oath of testimony, and the oath of a deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the closing of מי שקינא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These seven texts may be said in any language.

steps.title: Things that must be said only in Hebrew
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a second list: eight things that must be said in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: These must be said in לשון הקודש: the ביכורים reading, חליצה, the blessings and curses, ברכת כהנים, the כהן גדול's blessing, the king's portion, the עגלה ערופה portion, and the משוח מלחמה when he speaks to the people.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite list. These texts count only if they are said in Hebrew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list is the reverse of the first one. For these texts, the Hebrew words themselves are required. The משנה will next show where this rule comes from, starting with the first two items on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy language, Hebrew
The verses a person reads when he brings his first fruits to the מקדש
The ceremony that frees a יבמה when her husband's brother will not marry her
The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
The כהן anointed to speak to the army before battle

phrases.english: And these are said in the holy language:
the reading of first fruits, and חליצה,
the blessings and curses, the Priestly Blessing,
and the blessing of the כהן גדול, and the portion of the king,
and the portion of the calf whose neck is broken,

phrases.aramaic: וּמְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם.
phrases.english: and the one anointed for war at the time he speaks to the people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite list to the one in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These eight texts must be said in לשון הקודש.

steps.title: Why the first fruits reading must be in Hebrew
steps.stepSummary: The משנה learns that מקרא ביכורים must be in Hebrew by comparing the words 'וענית ואמרת' to 'וענו הלוים ואמרו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this about the ביכורים reading? The פסוק says 'And you shall answer and say before ה׳ your God,' and later it says 'And the לוים shall answer and say.' Just as there it was in Hebrew, so too here it must be in Hebrew.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives a source for the first item on the Hebrew-only list, the ביכורים reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, 'answer and say,' appear for the ביכורים and for the לוים at the blessings and curses. Since the לוים spoke in Hebrew, the matching words teach that the ביכורים reading must be in Hebrew too.

keyTerms.meaning: How? Here it means: how do we know this?
And you shall answer and say
And further on, meaning in another place in the תורה
Just as there, so too here. This is the formula for learning one case from the other.

phrases.english: The reading of first fruits, how?
phrases.notes: He means: how do we know it has to be in Hebrew?

phrases.english: "And you shall answer and say before ה׳ your God,"
and further on it says:
"And the Levites shall answer and say."
Just as there it is in the holy language,
so too here it is in the holy language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the first item in the step 7 list.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that מקרא ביכורים must be said in לשון הקודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared words וענית ואמרת (דברים 26:5) and וענו הלוים ואמרו (דברים 27:14).

steps.title: Why חליצה must be in Hebrew
steps.stepSummary: The משנה uses the same comparison for חליצה: 'וענתה ואמרה' matches 'וענו הלוים ואמרו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know this about חליצה? The פסוק says 'And she shall answer and say,' and later it says 'And the לוים shall answer and say.' Just as there it was in Hebrew, so too here it must be in Hebrew.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the source for the second item, חליצה, using exactly the same method as for ביכורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the חליצה ceremony, the woman's words are introduced with 'answer and say.' These are the same words used for the לוים. So her words, like theirs, must be said in Hebrew.

keyTerms.meaning: And she shall answer and say. These words are said about the יבמה at חליצה.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two lists: things that may be said in any language, and things that must be said in Hebrew. For ביכורים and חליצה, the Hebrew rule is learned from the words 'answer and say,' which also describe the לוים, who spoke in Hebrew.

phrases.english: חליצה, how?
"And she shall answer and say,"
and further on it says:
"And the Levites shall answer and say."
Just as there it is in the holy language,
so too here it is in the holy language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same comparison as step 8 for the next item on the list.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the words said at חליצה must be in לשון הקודש.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared words וענתה ואמרה (דברים 25:9) and וענו הלוים ואמרו (דברים 27:14).

steps.title: רבי יהודה's own source for חליצה in Hebrew
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns from the word 'ככה' that the words of חליצה must be said exactly in this language.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the פסוק says 'And she shall answer and say: So (ככה)…'. That means it is not valid until she says it in this exact language.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different source than the one in step 9 for why חליצה must be in לשון הקודש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first source compared the words 'וענתה ואמרה' to the לוים. רבי יהודה instead reads the word 'ככה' ('like this') as meaning she must say the words exactly as written, in Hebrew. Both reach the same result through a different reading of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives his own source here
'Like this' / 'so'. רבי יהודה reads it as 'in exactly these words'
In this language (Hebrew)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"And she shall answer and say: So [shall be done]"
phrases.notes: דברים 25:9. His whole proof rests on the last word, כָּכָה, 'like this'.

phrases.english: [it is not valid] until she says it in this language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent source for the same rule as step 9
steps.raayaObject: That חליצה must be said in לשון הקודש
steps.whatToRemember: חליצה must be in Hebrew. The first view learns it from 'וענתה ואמרה', and רבי יהודה learns it from 'ככה'.

steps.title: Where the blessings and curses took place
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts explaining the ברכות וקללות ceremony: after crossing the ירדן, Israel came to הר גריזים and הר עיבל, near שכם and אלוני מורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How were the blessings and curses done? When Israel crossed the ירדן, they came to הר גריזים and הר עיבל. These are in שומרון, next to שכם, near the oaks of מורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to the next item on its Hebrew-only list, ברכות וקללות, and begins by telling us where the ceremony happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question 'כיצד' is not a challenge. It is the משנה's way of opening a description. The location given here (near שכם) will be proven in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessings and curses said at the two mountains
How? The משנה uses it to open a description
The mountain of the blessings
The mountain of the curses
The oaks of מורה, a landmark near שכם

phrases.english: The blessings and curses, how [were they done]?
Once Israel crossed the Jordan

phrases.aramaic: וּבָאוּ אֶל הַר גְּרִיזִים וְאֶל הַר עֵיבָל
phrases.english: and came to Mount Gerizim and to Mount Ebal
which are in Shomron, which are beside Shechem,
which is near the oaks of Moreh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from חליצה to the next item on the list of things said in לשון הקודש
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ceremony took place at הר גריזים and הר עיבל, next to שכם, near אלוני מורה

steps.title: Proving the mountains are near שכם
steps.stepSummary: The משנה proves the location by matching 'אלון מורה' in דברים to 'אלון מורה' in the story of אברם, which is clearly at שכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק about the mountains says they are 'beyond the ירדן… near אלוני מורה'. Elsewhere it says 'אברם passed through the land until the place of שכם, until אלון מורה'. Just as אלון מורה there is שכם, so too אלון מורה here is שכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a proof for the location it just gave: that the mountains are next to שכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים mentions אלון מורה but not שכם. The פסוק about אברם puts אלון מורה together with שכם. Since it is the same landmark name, it must be the same place, so the mountains are near שכם.

keyTerms.meaning: There, meaning in another place in the תורה
'Just as… so too…', a pattern for comparing two פסוקים
The city near the two mountains

phrases.english: As it is said: "Are they not beyond the Jordan, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 11:30. The end of this פסוק, not quoted here, says 'near אלוני מורה'.

phrases.english: And elsewhere it says:
"And Avram passed through the land

phrases.aramaic: עַד מְקוֹם שְׁכֶם עַד אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה״.
phrases.english: until the place of Shechem, until the oak of Moreh."

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה הָאָמוּר לְהַלָּן — שְׁכֶם,
phrases.english: Just as the oak of Moreh mentioned there is Shechem,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֵלוֹן מוֹרֶה הָאָמוּר כָּאן — שְׁכֶם.
phrases.english: so too the oak of Moreh mentioned here is Shechem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the location stated in step 11
steps.raayaObject: That הר גריזים and הר עיבל are next to שכם
steps.raayaSupportSource: Matching 'אלון מורה' in דברים 11:30 and בראשית 12:6

steps.title: How the people stood at the mountains
steps.stepSummary: Six tribes stood on each mountain, while the כהנים, לוים and ארון stood below in the middle, arranged in circles, as the פסוק in יהושע describes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six tribes went up to the top of הר גריזים and six to the top of הר עיבל. The כהנים, the לוים and the ארון stood below in the middle. The כהנים circled the ארון, the לוים circled the כהנים, and the rest of Israel stood on both sides. This is as the פסוק says: 'All Israel… stood on this side and that side of the ארון'.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the setup of the ceremony: who stood where.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three layers in the valley: the ארון in the center, then a ring of כהנים, then a ring of לוים. The other tribes are split on the two mountains. The פסוק from יהושע backs up the picture of Israel standing on both sides of the ארון.

keyTerms.meaning: Six tribes
The Ark of the Covenant
Surround
On this side and on that side

phrases.aramaic: שִׁשָּׁה שְׁבָטִים עָלוּ לְרֹאשׁ הַר גְּרִיזִים
phrases.english: Six tribes went up to the top of Mount Gerizim

phrases.aramaic: וְשִׁשָּׁה שְׁבָטִים עָלוּ לְרֹאשׁ הַר עֵיבָל,
phrases.english: and six tribes went up to the top of Mount Ebal,
and the Kohanim, the Leviim, and the Ark
were standing below, in the middle.
The Kohanim surround the Ark,
and the Leviim [surround] the Kohanim,
and all Israel on this side and on that side,
as it is said: "And all Israel and its elders
and officers and its judges
standing on this side and on that side of the Ark, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: שִׁשָּׁה שְׁבָטִים עָלוּ לְרֹאשׁ הַר גְּרִיזִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the description of the ceremony, from where it happened to how the people stood
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Six tribes on each mountain; the ארון in the middle, circled by the כהנים, who were circled by the לוים

steps.title: How each blessing and curse was said
steps.stepSummary: Facing הר גריזים, they said a blessing ('ברוך האיש…'). Facing הר עיבל, they said the matching curse ('ארור האיש…'). Both sides answered 'אמן' each time, until all were finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: They turned toward הר גריזים and began with a blessing: 'Blessed is the man who does not make a carved or molten idol', and everyone answered 'אמן'. Then they turned toward הר עיבל and began with the curse: 'Cursed is the man who makes a carved or molten idol', and everyone answered 'אמן'. They went on like this until they finished all the blessings and curses.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the actual saying of the blessings and curses, back and forth between the two mountains.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each curse in the תורה was paired with a matching blessing that was said first. The speakers faced the mountain the line was aimed at. Both groups, on both mountains, answered 'אמן' to every line, blessing and curse alike.

keyTerms.meaning: They turned their faces
A carved idol and a molten (cast) idol
Cursed
These and those, meaning both groups

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think only one mountain answered each line. The משנה says 'אלו ואלו', so both sides answered 'אמן' to the blessings and to the curses.
steps.whatToRemember: At הר גריזים and הר עיבל every curse was matched by a blessing said first. Each time, both mountains answered 'אמן', until all were done.

phrases.english: They turned their faces toward Mount Gerizim
phrases.notes: The משנה doesn't say who 'they' are here; it means the group standing in the middle.

phrases.english: and opened with the blessing:

phrases.aramaic: ״בָּרוּךְ הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַעֲשֶׂה פֶסֶל וּמַסֵּכָה״,
phrases.english: "Blessed is the man who does not make a carved or molten idol,"
and these and those answer "Amen."
They turned their faces toward Mount Ebal
and opened with the curse:
"Cursed is the man who makes a carved or molten idol,"
and these and those answer "Amen,"
until they finish the blessings and curses.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָפְכוּ פְּנֵיהֶם כְּלַפֵּי הַר גְּרִיזִים וּפָתְחוּ בִּבְרָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing the setup, the משנה describes the ceremony itself
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each blessing was said facing הר גריזים and each curse facing הר עיבל, with both sides answering 'אמן' to all of them

steps.title: Building the altar and writing the תורה on it
steps.stepSummary: After the blessings and curses, they brought stones, built a מזבח, plastered it, and wrote all the words of the תורה on it in seventy languages.
steps.simpleTranslation: After that, they brought the stones, built the altar, covered it with plaster, and wrote on it all the words of the תורה in seventy languages.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us the next stage of the ceremony: building a מזבח and writing the whole תורה on its stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the ceremony was all spoken words: blessings, curses, and 'אמן.' Now it moves to physical actions: building, plastering, and writing. The surprising new detail is that the writing was in seventy languages, not only in לשון הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Altar
Plaster or lime, used to coat the stones
And they plastered it
Seventy languages, meaning the languages of all the nations

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that the תורה was written in seventy languages shows that its message was meant to be understood by every nation, not only by בני ישראל.

phrases.english: And afterward they brought the stones,
and built the altar,
and plastered it with plaster,

in seventy languages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the order of the ceremony right after the blessings and curses of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: They built a plastered מזבח of stones and wrote the entire תורה on it in seventy languages.

steps.title: Proof for seventy languages from 'very clearly'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה proves the seventy languages from the פסוק 'באר היטב', which means the writing must be very clear.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a פסוק to back up the claim that the תורה was written in seventy languages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to write the תורה on the stones 'באר היטב', which means 'very clearly explained.' The משנה reads this as clear to everyone, so it must be written in every language. That is the source for the seventy languages in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said, introducing a פסוק as proof
Explain very clearly

phrases.english: As it is said: "very clearly."
phrases.notes: דברים 27:8. 'Clear' is read as clear to everyone, which means writing it in every language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the seventy-languages detail in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the תורה on the stones was written in seventy languages.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in דברים 27:8, 'באר היטב', meaning 'very clearly.'

steps.title: They took the stones and moved on
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts the next stage: they took the stones and came to another place. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they took the stones, and came…
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins describing what happened to the stones after the writing. It is setting up the next part of the story, which continues in the coming lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the writing is done, the stones are taken along and the people move on. This step only opens the sentence, and the details of where they went come next.

keyTerms.meaning: And they took
And they came

phrases.english: And they took the stones,
and came

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story forward after the writing on the stones in steps 15–16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After writing the תורה on them, they took the stones and moved on (the sentence continues).
